title: Caibarién candy-seller fine protest and municipal-office follow-up
location: Caibarién, Villa Clara; reports also describe a later visit to the municipal People’s Power office, with the gathering boundary unresolved
participants_original: Periódico Cubano reports several dozen witnesses gathering around the seller on February 27; ADN Cuba reports dozens at the municipal People’s Power office on February 28. The accounts may describe overlapping participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Both opened accounts use qualitative terms, several dozen or dozens, without a count proving at least 50. Witnesses are not necessarily all demonstrators, and the office visit may be a separate action.

dates.summary: Periódico Cubano dates the seller-side gathering to the morning of February 27. ADN Cuba describes dozens going to the municipal office on February 28. Whether this is one continuing episode or two actions is unresolved.

location_organizer.summary: Reports place the seller-side gathering in Caibarién and mention a later municipal People’s Power office visit. No organizer is identified.

demands.summary: Accounts describe opposition to two DIS fines totaling 2,000 pesos and a demand to cancel the penalty. The provisional political_behavior_process category reflects a demand about state enforcement, pending coordinator review.

participants.summary: The two opened accounts say several dozen or dozens, but do not establish a minimum of 50 or whether those described at both locations are separate or overlapping groups.

state_response.accommodation.summary: ADN Cuba says authorities removed the reported 2,000-peso fine. This is a reported accommodation if the office action belongs to the same episode.

protester_violence.summary: The article's reference to police vehicles not appearing in videos does not establish whether protesters used violence; value remains unknown.

unknown_fields.summary: End date, event boundary, organizer, exact count, event-specific arrest/force details, and the unreported response categories remain unknown.

notes: Periódico Cubano describes a gathering around a seller after two DIS fines totaling 2,000 pesos and a later video of him going toward municipal government to protest. ADN Cuba dates a visit by dozens to the municipal office one day later and reports that authorities removed the fine. That February 28 outcome is attributed to the office action and must not be transferred to the February 27 seller-side gathering unless they are established as one episode. The taxonomy mapping is provisional; no search-only lead is treated as body-confirmed evidence.
open_questions: Establish the number of actual demonstrators at each location and whether any gathering reached 50.
Resolve February 27 versus February 28, whether the office visit was a separate public assembly, and the episode boundary.
Verify the municipal outcome and the exact Radio Televisión Martí report or other written origin; assess source independence.
Review the provisional demand-category mapping against the coordinator’s codebook.

title: Camagüey queue leafleting and arrests associated with La cola de la libertad
location: Queue outside an MLC store in Camagüey; exact store and street unknown
organizer: Activists distributing leaflets associated with La cola de la libertad; names unknown
participants_original: CiberCuba says almost half a dozen leaflet distributors were arrested and people in the queue objected; no total number of demonstrators or participating bystanders is given.
threshold_50_evidence: The article counts neither the leafleters as a group nor participating bystanders. Arrests and the size of the queue cannot establish 50 demonstrators.

dates.summary: CiberCuba dates the episode to Saturday, February 27, 2021.

location_organizer.summary: The article describes activists distributing leaflets from La cola de la libertad at a queue outside an MLC store in Camagüey; it does not name the store, street, or activists.

demands.summary: The report identifies leaflet distribution about La cola de la libertad and a correction says the arrests were for distributing leaflets, not simply chanting a slogan. Exact leaflet text and an explicit demand directed at Cuban authorities or policy are not established.

participants.summary: Almost half a dozen arrests and unspecified objections from people in the queue are reported; neither provides a total for demonstrators.

state_response.arrests.summary: The report says police arrested several leaflet distributors. It describes people being dragged or carried, but does not establish beatings.

unknown_fields.summary: Total attendance, participating bystander count, exact leaflet content, actual end, crowd dispersal, demonstrator violence, and response categories beyond reported arrests remain unknown.

notes: The article corrects its earlier framing: the reported arrests concerned distributing leaflets about La cola de la libertad, not merely chanting Patria y Vida. A separate CIVICUS search result describes a February 28 demonstration against long queues, but its body was not read and its relation to this February 27 report is unresolved. The entire queue is not counted as participating.
open_questions: Recover the leaflet wording and establish a specific demand directed at the Cuban government or its policy.
Establish the number of leafleters and whether any queue members joined a public assembly of at least 50.
Resolve the date, physical end, and relationship among this account and search-only Camagüey reports.
Clarify the arrests and force used from an original or independent account; dragging or carrying alone does not establish beating.
